mcqs.q: Chemically, gypsum rock is:
mcqs.explain: Heating (calcination) drives off part of the water of crystallization to give calcium sulfate hemihydrate.

mcqs.q: All three gypsum products (plaster, stone, improved stone) are chemically:
mcqs.explain: They differ only in the method of calcination, which changes crystal form, density and water demand.

mcqs.q: A replica on which a restoration or prosthesis is fabricated is called a:
mcqs.explain: A model is used to plan treatment and observe progress; a die is a reproduction of a prepared tooth; a cast is more accurate than a study model.

mcqs.q: A die is defined as:
opts: A reproduction of a prepared tooth
A replica of the whole arch
mcqs.explain: Casts, models and dies are positive replicas obtained from negative reproductions (impressions).

mcqs.q: Calcination is best defined as:
opts: Heating a solid material to drive off chemically combined components such as water
mcqs.explain: Calcination of gypsum removes part of the water of crystallization to produce hemihydrate.

mcqs.q: Dental PLASTER is produced by heating gypsum in an:
opts: Open kettle at 110/120 °C, giving beta hemihydrate
Autoclave with steam at 125 °C, giving alpha hemihydrate
mcqs.explain: Beta hemihydrate has irregular, very porous, randomly shaped crystals.

mcqs.q: Which crystal characteristics belong to dental PLASTER?
opts: Irregular shaped, very porous, random shaped
Cubic or rectangular and very dense
mcqs.explain: Its porosity is why plaster needs the most gauging water and is the weakest product.

mcqs.q: Dental STONE is produced by:
opts: Steam under pressure at 125 °C, giving alpha hemihydrate
mcqs.explain: Alpha hemihydrate has more uniform, denser, larger crystals with smoother particles.

mcqs.q: Improved (high-strength) stone is produced by:
opts: Boiling gypsum in 30% calcium chloride solution at 100 °C
mcqs.explain: It yields very dense, cubic or rectangular, large alpha-hemihydrate crystals.

mcqs.q: Type II gypsum in ADA Specification No. 25 is:
mcqs.explain: Type I impression plaster, Type II model plaster, Type III dental stone, Type IV high strength, Type V high strength/high expansion.

mcqs.q: Type V gypsum is dental stone that is:
mcqs.explain: Type IV is high strength; Type V adds high expansion.

mcqs.q: When hemihydrate is mixed with water, the setting reaction:
opts: Converts it back to dihydrate and liberates heat
Converts it to anhydrite and absorbs heat
Is purely physical with no chemical change
mcqs.explain: CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½H₂O → CaSO₄·2H₂O + heat — an exothermic hydration.

mcqs.q: The average water/powder ratio for STONE is:
mcqs.explain: Plaster 45–50 ml/100 g; stone 28–30; improved stone 19–24 ml/100 g.

mcqs.q: Which product requires the LEAST gauging water?
mcqs.explain: Less water demand corresponds to denser crystals and greater strength.

mcqs.q: Working time (initial setting time) is the period from the start of the mix until the mass:
opts: Becomes rigid and separable from the impression
mcqs.explain: It represents the time available for manipulating the product and indicates partial progress of the setting reaction.

mcqs.q: Final setting time indicates:
opts: The major completion of the setting reaction, when the mass is rigid and can be separated
The moment surface gloss is lost
The time to reach dry strength
mcqs.explain: The mass becomes rigid and can be separated from the impression.

mcqs.q: Setting times are usually measured by a surface penetration test using:
mcqs.explain: The ¼-lb needle marks initial set and the 1-lb needle marks final set — each time is reached when its needle no longer makes an indentation.

mcqs.q: The 1-lb Gillmore needle is used to determine the:
mcqs.explain: The ¼-lb needle determines the initial setting time.

mcqs.q: Loss of surface gloss indicates the initial (working) set and typically occurs at:
mcqs.explain: Final set takes about 30 to 45 minutes.

mcqs.q: Which change will SLOW the setting reaction?
mcqs.explain: Slower set: decreased mixing, higher W/P ratio, and retarders such as borax.

mcqs.q: A commonly used RETARDER for gypsum products is:
mcqs.explain: Potassium sulfate is the commonly used accelerator.

mcqs.q: A commonly used ACCELERATOR is:
mcqs.explain: Accelerated set also results from increased mixing and a lower water/powder ratio.

mcqs.q: Regarding mixing time and setting time:
opts: The longer the mixing time, the shorter the setting time
The longer the mixing time, the longer the setting time
mcqs.explain: More spatulation breaks up forming crystals and creates more nuclei, hastening the set.

mcqs.q: Hygroscopic setting expansion is the expansion that occurs when gypsum sets:
mcqs.explain: It is greater than normal setting expansion and is used to increase the setting expansion of casting investments.

mcqs.q: Which product shows the GREATEST normal setting expansion?
mcqs.explain: High-strength stone expands the least, which is why it is used for accurate dies.

mcqs.q: The normal setting expansion of high-strength stone is:
mcqs.explain: Plaster 0.2–0.3%, stone 0.08–0.10%, high-strength stone 0.05–0.07%.

mcqs.q: The strength of a gypsum product is usually measured as its:
mcqs.explain: Improved stone is strongest, stone intermediate and plaster weakest — plaster needs the most gauging water.

mcqs.q: Which sequence correctly ranks strength from WEAKEST to STRONGEST?
mcqs.explain: Water demand is inversely related to strength.

mcqs.q: Wet strength is also known as:
mcqs.explain: Dry strength is reached once excess water has evaporated and is considerably higher.

mcqs.q: Regarding the water/powder ratio and strength:
opts: Thicker mixes increase strength within limits; thinner mixes decrease it
The ratio does not affect strength
mcqs.explain: Excess water leaves porosity in the set mass, lowering strength.

mcqs.q: The greatest surface hardness occurs when the product reaches its:
mcqs.explain: Casts and dies should set 1–2 hours, preferably overnight or longer, before laboratory procedures.

mcqs.q: Why should a gypsum cast NOT be soaked in plain water for prolonged periods?
opts: Gypsum is slightly soluble and the surface may dissolve away
It will become too hard to trim
mcqs.explain: When soaking is needed, slurry water (already saturated with calcium sulfate) is used instead.

mcqs.q: The correct mixing method for gypsum products is to:
opts: Add the measured water to the bowl first, then gradually add the powder
Add the powder first and then pour water on top
Mix the powder dry before adding water
mcqs.explain: Adding water first and sifting powder into it reduces air entrapment; a smooth homogeneous mix takes about 1 minute.

mcqs.q: A dental vibrator is used during mixing and pouring mainly to:
opts: Reduce air bubbles in the mix and during filling
mcqs.explain: The mixture should flow slowly 'ahead of itself' to prevent air entrapment.

mcqs.q: After pouring, the dental stone model should be left undisturbed for:
opts: Only until the gloss is lost
mcqs.explain: It is then separated from the impression; laboratory work should wait until dry strength (1–2 hours, ideally overnight).

saqs.q: Describe how dental plaster, dental stone and improved stone are produced, and give the crystal characteristics of each.
saqs.a: All three are calcium sulfate hemihydrate produced by calcination of gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate). Dental plaster: gypsum heated in an OPEN KETTLE at 110/120 °C, giving BETA calcium sulfate hemihydrate with irregular-shaped, very porous, randomly shaped crystals. Dental stone: gypsum heated with STEAM UNDER PRESSURE at 125 °C, giving ALPHA calcium sulfate hemihydrate with more uniform shaped crystals that are more dense than plaster, larger and with smoother particles. Improved (high-strength) stone: gypsum boiled in a 30% CALCIUM CHLORIDE solution at 100 °C, also giving ALPHA hemihydrate but with very dense, cubic or rectangular, large crystals.

saqs.q: List the five ADA types of gypsum products and the average water/powder ratio of plaster, stone and improved stone.
saqs.a: ADA Specification No. 25 classifies five types: Type I impression plaster; Type II model plaster; Type III dental stone; Type IV dental stone, high strength; and Type V dental stone, high strength and high expansion. Average water/powder ratios: plaster 45–50 ml per 100 g (0.45–0.50), stone 28–30 ml per 100 g (0.28–0.30), and improved stone 19–24 ml per 100 g (0.19–0.24). The denser the crystals, the less gauging water is needed and the stronger the set product.

saqs.q: Define initial and final setting time and explain how each is measured.
saqs.a: Working time (initial setting time) is the length of time from the start of the mix until the setting mass reaches a semihard stage; it represents the time available for manipulating the product and indicates partial progress of the setting reaction. Final setting time is the length of time from the start of the mix until the setting mass becomes rigid and can be separated from the impression, indicating the major completion of the setting reaction. Setting times are usually measured with a surface penetration test using Gillmore needles: the initial setting time is reached when the surface supports the weight of the ¼-lb needle and the final setting time when it supports the 1-lb needle — that is, when the respective needle no longer makes an indentation. Clinically, loss of surface gloss marks the initial (working) set at typically 5 to 7 minutes, and final set takes 30 to 45 minutes.

saqs.q: List the ways to increase and to decrease the setting time of gypsum products.
saqs.a: To INCREASE the setting time (a slower-setting product): decreased mixing, a higher water/powder ratio which creates a thinner mix, and the addition of chemicals called retarders — a commonly used retarder is borax. To DECREASE the setting time (a faster-setting product): increased mixing, since the longer the mixing time the shorter the setting time; a lower water/powder ratio which creates a thicker mix; and the addition of chemicals called accelerators — a commonly used accelerator is potassium sulfate.

saqs.q: Describe setting expansion and strength of gypsum products, including the figures.
saqs.a: Normal setting expansion is the expansion that occurs when gypsum sets in air, and all gypsum products expand normally on setting: plaster expands the most at 0.2% to 0.3%, stone expands 0.08% to 0.10%, and high-strength stone expands the least at 0.05% to 0.07%. Hygroscopic setting expansion is the expansion that occurs when gypsum sets while immersed in water; it is greater and can be used to increase the setting expansion of casting investments. Strength is usually measured as compressive strength. Plaster, which requires the most gauging water to make a fluid mix, is the weakest; improved stone is the strongest and stone is intermediate. Two types of strength are recognised, wet (green) strength and dry strength. Strength depends on the water/powder ratio: thicker mixes increase strength within limits and thinner mixes decrease it. The greatest surface hardness occurs when the product reaches its dry strength, so casts and dies should be allowed to set for 1 to 2 hours, preferably overnight or longer, before laboratory procedures.

saqs.q: Outline the technique of mixing and pouring a gypsum product.
saqs.a: The technique requires only a mixing bowl, a mixing spatula, room-temperature water and the gypsum product. The measured WATER is added into the mixing bowl FIRST, followed by gradual addition of the powder. Hand mixing is done in a rubber bowl with a spatula to combine powder and water; the mix should be smooth, homogeneous, workable and free of air bubbles, and use of a dental vibrator will reduce bubbles. A smooth homogeneous mix is obtained in approximately 1 minute. When filling the impression, the gypsum mixture must flow slowly 'ahead of itself' to prevent entrapment of air, which is usually accomplished with a dental vibrator. The model is then left undisturbed for 45 to 60 minutes until the material has set completely, after which the gypsum model is separated from the impression. Because gypsum is slightly soluble in water, prolonged soaking in plain water can dissolve the surface, so slurry water is used when soaking is required.
